app.title: Time calculator
app.description: Enter times as digits only (HMM or HHMM, e.g. 930, 1000). The hyphen is fixed between the fields; after the first time is complete, focus moves to the second automatically.

forward.title: Forward
forward.description: Go from first time to second time.

backward.title: Backward
backward.description: Go from second time back to first time.

usage.title: How to use
usage.step1: Type the first time as digits only: HMM or HHMM (for example 930 or 1000).
usage.step2: The second field is focused automatically once the first time is complete, or press Enter / → to move on.
usage.step3: Read the Forward and Backward results and tap the copy icon next to any value.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: What is the difference between Forward and Backward?
faq.a1: Forward counts clockwise from the first time to the second; Backward counts the other way around. For 0300 to 2000 that is 17:00 forward and 7:00 backward.
faq.q2: How are times across midnight handled?
faq.a2: Each result wraps within a single 24-hour day. Going forward from 23:00 to 06:00 is 7:00, and backward is 17:00.
faq.a3: When pasting, yes: 10:05 pm, 10:5pm and 1005pm are all understood. When typing, enter digits only (2205).
faq.q4: Do I need to type a colon or a space?
faq.a4: No. The dash between the two fields is fixed; just type 3 or 4 digits for each time.
faq.a5: No. All calculations run in your browser. Only your language choice is saved locally, and ads are served by Google as described in the privacy policy.
faq.a6: Times are treated as plain local clock times, with no time zone or daylight-saving conversion.

about.title: About this calculator
about.body: This tool computes the elapsed time between two clock times within the same day. Forward gives the shortest clockwise span to the second time; Backward gives the complementary span in the opposite direction. Because only the time of day is known, no date, time zone or daylight-saving adjustments are applied.
